findings.issue: The override 403 is documented as an 'empty body / пустое тело (no leak)'. Empirically the body is NOT empty — it is the standard error envelope {"error":{"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"viewing another subject's SoD conflicts requires admin/owner authority"}} (router.ts sendErrorEnvelope). The security property that actually holds and matters (no subjectId/conflicts/heldRoles, no exists-oracle, static message) is fully satisfied — only the wording 'empty body' is imprecise.
findings.suggestion: Reword the ADR/handoff to 'static generic 403 envelope carrying no subject data / no exists-oracle' instead of 'empty body'. Pure documentation nit; no code change.

findings.issue: The LIST gate (assertApproverIsHuman) admits ANY active human, so every active human can enumerate the ENTIRE tenant's pending dual-control queue (proposed_by, role display_name, resource_type, operation, scope of every semi-confirmed grant/assignment). This is deliberate and CORRECT — it is exactly the write-path eligibility (approve/reject on this same file use the identical assertApproverIsHuman) and is grounded in T-0044 ADR §9 (any distinct active human may be the second approver). Read bar == write bar, so no privilege escalation. Flagging only because the exposure is broad and worth an explicit acknowledgement.
findings.suggestion: None required for this task. If tenants later want a narrower approver pool, that is a policy change to the dual-control model (T-0044), not a defect here.
